judged_text: TopicRetriever executes the scheduled PollFeed job inline per embed request (lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})), bypassing Sidekiq; because the throttle key is per embed URL (retrieved:#{@embed_url}) rather than per feed, a site with k embedded articles can trigger up to k full feed fetches plus N import attempts per minute instead of the intended hourly poll, and any PollFeed exception now also fails RetrieveTopic with its retries re-polling the feed — this job-layer coupling should be an enqueue or a check against cached feed data, not an inline execute

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calling the scheduled job inline (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` in lib/topic_retriever.rb) when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, which bypasses Sidekiq scheduling/retry settings. It also shows throttling in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? is keyed by embed URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so many distinct embedded URLs can each trigger an inline PollFeed run (and therefore repeated `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed) within the throttle window. This is a concrete architectural/performance/coupling concern grounded in the diff, though it’s not strictly a functional correctness defect in isolation.
